Why is the sky blue?

Sunlight looks white, but it is made of all visible wavelengths. When sunlight enters the Earth's atmosphere, it meets air molecules that are much smaller than the wavelength of visible light.

This interaction is called Rayleigh scattering. Rayleigh scattering scatters short wavelengths, such as blue light, far more strongly than long wavelengths, such as red light.

Because blue light is scattered in all directions across the sky, the sky appears blue when you look away from the Sun.

At sunset, sunlight travels through a much longer path of atmosphere. Most of the blue light is scattered away before it reaches your eyes, so the Sun and the horizon look red or orange.
